passages.text: Now in those days the Philistines gathered their forces for warfare against Israel. So Achish said to David, “You must understand that you and your men are to go out to battle with me.”
passages.sermon:
The Philistines were a nation that often fought against Israel.
In those days, the Philistines gathered their army.
They prepared for war against Israel.
Achish was a Philistine ruler.
Achish spoke to David.
David was living among the Philistines at that time.
Achish said to David, “You must understand this.”
“You and your men will go out to battle with me.”
passages.original: וַֽיְהִי֙ בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם וַיִּקְבְּצ֨וּ פְלִשְׁתִּ֤ים אֶת־ מַֽחֲנֵיהֶם֙ לַצָּבָ֔א לְהִלָּחֵ֖ם בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אָכִישׁ֙ אֶל־ דָּוִ֔ד יָדֹ֣עַ תֵּדַ֗ע כִּ֤י אִתִּי֙ תֵּצֵ֣א בַֽמַּחֲנֶ֔ה אַתָּ֖ה וַאֲנָשֶֽׁיךָ׃

passages.text: David replied, “Then you will come to know what your servant can do.” “Very well,” said Achish. “I will make you my bodyguard for life.”
passages.sermon:
David was a servant of Achish, the Philistine king.
Achish trusted David.
Achish believed David had become an enemy to Israel.
Achish wanted David to fight with him against Israel.
David spoke to Achish.
David said, “You will see what your servant can do.”
Achish answered David.
Achish said, “I will make you my bodyguard for life.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר דָּוִד֙ אֶל־ אָכִ֔ישׁ לָכֵן֙ אַתָּ֣ה תֵדַ֔ע אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־ יַעֲשֶׂ֖ה עַבְדֶּ֑ךָ וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אָכִישׁ֙ אֶל־ דָּוִ֔ד לָכֵ֗ן שֹׁמֵ֧ר לְרֹאשִׁ֛י אֲשִֽׂימְךָ֖ כָּל־ הַיָּמִֽים׃פ

passages.text: Now by this time Samuel had died, and all Israel had mourned for him and buried him in Ramah, his own city. And Saul had removed the mediums and spiritists from the land.
passages.sermon:
Samuel was a prophet in Israel.
Samuel had died.
All Israel mourned for Samuel.
They buried Samuel in Ramah.
Ramah was Samuel’s own city.
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul removed the mediums from the land.
Saul also removed the spiritists from the land.
passages.original: וּשְׁמוּאֵ֣ל מֵ֔ת וַיִּסְפְּדוּ־ לוֹ֙ כָּל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיִּקְבְּרֻ֥הוּ בָרָמָ֖ה וּבְעִיר֑וֹ וְשָׁא֗וּל הֵסִ֛יר הָאֹב֥וֹת וְאֶת־ הַיִּדְּעֹנִ֖ים מֵהָאָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: The Philistines came together and camped at Shunem, while Saul gathered all Israel and camped at Gilboa.
passages.sermon:
The Philistines were Israel’s enemies.
The Philistines gathered their army.
They came to the land of Israel.
The Philistines set up camp at Shunem.
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul gathered all the men of Israel.
Saul and the Israelites set up camp at Gilboa.
passages.original: וַיִּקָּבְצ֣וּ פְלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ וַיַּחֲנ֣וּ בְשׁוּנֵ֑ם וַיִּקְבֹּ֤ץ שָׁאוּל֙ אֶת־ כָּל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בַּגִּלְבֹּֽעַ׃

passages.text: When Saul saw the Philistine army, he was afraid and trembled violently.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul saw the Philistine army.
Saul became afraid.
Saul’s heart trembled very much.
passages.original: וַיַּ֥רְא שָׁא֖וּל אֶת־ מַחֲנֵ֣ה פְלִשְׁתִּ֑ים וַיִּרָ֕א וַיֶּחֱרַ֥ד לִבּ֖וֹ מְאֹֽד׃

passages.text: He inquired of the LORD, but the LORD did not answer him by dreams or Urim or prophets.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul asked the LORD for guidance.
The LORD did not answer Saul.
The LORD did not speak to Saul in dreams.
The LORD did not answer Saul through the Urim.
The LORD did not speak to Saul by prophets.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁאַ֤ל שָׁאוּל֙ בַּֽיהוָ֔ה וְלֹ֥א עָנָ֖הוּ יְהוָ֑ה גַּ֧ם בַּחֲלֹמ֛וֹת גַּ֥ם בָּאוּרִ֖ים גַּ֥ם בַּנְּבִיאִֽם׃

passages.text: Then Saul said to his servants, “Find me a woman who is a medium, so I can go and consult her.” “There is a medium at Endor,” his servants replied.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul spoke to his servants.
He said, "Find a woman who is a medium."
He wanted to consult a medium.
He said, "I will go to her and ask her questions."
His servants answered him.
They said, "There is a woman who is a medium at Endor."
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר שָׁא֜וּל לַעֲבָדָ֗יו בַּקְּשׁוּ־ לִי֙ אֵ֣שֶׁת בַּעֲלַת־ א֔וֹב וְאֵלְכָ֥ה אֵלֶ֖יהָ וְאֶדְרְשָׁה־ בָּ֑הּ וַיֹּאמְר֤וּ עֲבָדָיו֙ אֵלָ֔יו הִנֵּ֛ה אֵ֥שֶׁת בַּֽעֲלַת־ א֖וֹב בְּעֵ֥ין דּֽוֹר׃

passages.text: So Saul disguised himself by putting on different clothes, and he set out with two of his men. They came to the woman at night, and Saul said, “Consult a spirit for me. Bring up for me the one I name.”
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul wanted to speak with a spirit.
Saul put on different clothes to hide his identity.
Saul disguised himself.
Two men went with Saul.
Saul and the two men traveled together.
They went to see a woman who was a medium.
They arrived at the woman's house at night.
Saul spoke to the woman.
Saul said, "Consult a spirit for me."
Saul said, "Bring up for me the person I tell you."
passages.original: וַיִּתְחַפֵּ֣שׂ שָׁא֗וּל וַיִּלְבַּשׁ֙ בְּגָדִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֔ים וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ ה֗וּא וּשְׁנֵ֤י אֲנָשִׁים֙ עִמּ֔וֹ וַיָּבֹ֥אוּ אֶל־ הָאִשָּׁ֖ה לָ֑יְלָה וַיֹּ֗אמֶר קָסוֹמִי נָ֥א לִי֙ בָּא֔וֹב וְהַ֣עֲלִי לִ֔י אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־ אֹמַ֖ר אֵלָֽיִךְ׃

passages.text: But the woman replied, “Surely you know what Saul has done, how he has killed the mediums and spiritists in the land. Why have you set a trap to get me killed?”
passages.sermon:
The woman spoke to Saul.
She said, “You know what Saul has done.”
Saul removed the mediums and spiritists from the land.
She asked, “Why do you set a trap for my life?”
She said, “Do you want to kill me?”
passages.original: וַתֹּ֨אמֶר הָֽאִשָּׁ֜ה אֵלָ֗יו הִנֵּ֨ה אַתָּ֤ה יָדַ֙עְתָּ֙ אֵ֣ת אֲשֶׁר־ עָשָׂ֣ה שָׁא֔וּל אֲשֶׁ֥ר הִכְרִ֛ית אֶת־ הָאֹב֥וֹת וְאֶת־ הַיִּדְּעֹנִ֖י מִן־ הָאָ֑רֶץ וְלָמָ֥ה אַתָּ֛ה מִתְנַקֵּ֥שׁ בְּנַפְשִׁ֖י לַהֲמִיתֵֽנִי׃

passages.text: Then Saul swore to her by the LORD: “As surely as the LORD lives, no punishment shall come upon you for this.”
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul spoke to the woman.
Saul made a promise to her.
Saul swore by the LORD.
Saul said, “As surely as the LORD lives, no punishment will come to you for this.”
passages.original: וַיִּשָּׁ֤בַֽע לָהּ֙ שָׁא֔וּל בַּֽיהוָ֖ה לֵאמֹ֑ר חַי־ יְהוָ֕ה אִֽם־ יִקְּרֵ֥ךְ עָוֺ֖ן בַּדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּֽה׃

passages.text: “Whom shall I bring up for you?” the woman asked. “Bring up Samuel,” he replied.
passages.sermon:
The woman spoke to Saul.
She asked, “Whom shall I bring up for you?”
Saul answered her.
He said, “Bring up Samuel for me.”
passages.original: וַתֹּ֙אמֶר֙ הָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה אֶת־ מִ֖י אַֽעֲלֶה־ לָּ֑ךְ וַיֹּ֕אמֶר אֶת־ שְׁמוּאֵ֖ל הַֽעֲלִי־ לִֽי׃

passages.text: But when the woman saw Samuel, she cried out in a loud voice and said to Saul, “Why have you deceived me? You are Saul!”
passages.sermon:
The woman saw Samuel.
She cried out with a loud voice.
She spoke to Saul.
She said, “Why have you deceived me?”
She said, “You are Saul!”
passages.original: וַתֵּ֤רֶא הָֽאִשָּׁה֙ אֶת־ שְׁמוּאֵ֔ל וַתִּזְעַ֖ק בְּק֣וֹל גָּד֑וֹל וַתֹּאמֶר֩ הָאִשָּׁ֨ה אֶל־ שָׁא֧וּל לֵאמֹ֛ר לָ֥מָּה רִמִּיתָ֖נִי וְאַתָּ֥ה שָׁאֽוּל׃

passages.text: “Do not be afraid,” the king replied. “What do you see?” “I see a god coming up out of the earth,” the woman answered.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king.
The woman was a medium at Endor.
Saul spoke to the woman.
Saul said, “Do not be afraid.”
Saul asked, “What do you see?”
The woman answered Saul.
The woman said, “I see a god coming up out of the earth.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר לָ֥הּ הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ אַל־ תִּֽירְאִ֖י כִּ֣י מָ֣ה רָאִ֑ית וַתֹּ֤אמֶר הָֽאִשָּׁה֙ אֶל־ שָׁא֔וּל אֱלֹהִ֥ים רָאִ֖יתִי עֹלִ֥ים מִן־ הָאָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: “What does he look like?” asked Saul. “An old man is coming up,” she replied. “And he is wearing a robe.” So Saul knew that it was Samuel, and he bowed facedown in reverence.
passages.sermon:
Saul spoke to the woman.
He asked, “What does he look like?”
The woman answered Saul.
She said, “An old man is coming up.”
She said, “He is wearing a robe.”
Saul understood this was Samuel.
Saul bowed down with his face to the ground.
Saul showed respect.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לָהּ֙ מַֽה־ תָּאֳר֔וֹ וַתֹּ֗אמֶר אִ֤ישׁ זָקֵן֙ עֹלֶ֔ה וְה֥וּא עֹטֶ֖ה מְעִ֑יל וַיֵּ֤דַע שָׁאוּל֙ כִּֽי־ שְׁמוּאֵ֣ל ה֔וּא וַיִּקֹּ֥ד אַפַּ֛יִם אַ֖רְצָה וַיִּשְׁתָּֽחוּ׃ס

passages.text: Then Samuel said to Saul, “Why have you disturbed me by bringing me up?” “I am deeply distressed,” replied Saul. “The Philistines are fighting against me, and God has turned away from me. He no longer answers me, either by prophets or by dreams. So I have called on you to tell me what to do.”
passages.sermon:
Samuel was a prophet of God who had died.
Saul was the king of Israel.
Samuel spoke to Saul.
Samuel said, “Why have you disturbed me by bringing me up?”
Saul replied to Samuel.
Saul said, “I am deeply distressed.”
Saul said, “The Philistines are fighting against me.”
Saul said, “God has turned away from me.”
Saul said, “God no longer answers me.”
Saul said, “God does not answer me by prophets.”
Saul said, “God does not answer me by dreams.”
Saul said, “I have called on you to tell me what to do.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר שְׁמוּאֵל֙ אֶל־ שָׁא֔וּל לָ֥מָּה הִרְגַּזְתַּ֖נִי לְהַעֲל֣וֹת אֹתִ֑י וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שָׁ֠אוּל צַר־ לִ֨י מְאֹ֜ד וּפְלִשְׁתִּ֣ים׀ נִלְחָמִ֣ים בִּ֗י וֵֽאלֹהִ֞ים סָ֤ר מֵֽעָלַי֙ וְלֹֽא־ עָנָ֣נִי ע֗וֹד גַּ֤ם בְּיַֽד־ הַנְּבִיאִם֙ גַּם־ בַּ֣חֲלֹמ֔וֹת וָאֶקְרָאֶ֣ה לְךָ֔ לְהוֹדִיעֵ֖נִי מָ֥ה אֶעֱשֶֽׂה׃ס

passages.text: “Why do you consult me,” asked Samuel, “since the LORD has turned away from you and become your enemy?
passages.sermon:
Samuel was a prophet of God.
\r\nSamuel spoke to Saul, the king of Israel.
\r\nSamuel said, “Why do you ask me?”
\r\nThe LORD has turned away from you.
\r\nThe LORD has become your enemy.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שְׁמוּאֵ֔ל וְלָ֖מָּה תִּשְׁאָלֵ֑נִי וַיהוָ֛ה סָ֥ר מֵעָלֶ֖יךָ וַיְהִ֥י עָרֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: He has done exactly what He spoke through me: The LORD has torn the kingship out of your hand and given it to your neighbor David.
passages.sermon: The LORD acted as He said He would through me.\r\nThe LORD took the kingship from you.\r\nThe LORD gave the kingship to your neighbor David.
passages.original: וַיַּ֤עַשׂ יְהוָה֙ ל֔וֹ כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר דִּבֶּ֣ר בְּיָדִ֑י וַיִּקְרַ֨ע יְהוָ֤ה אֶת־ הַמַּמְלָכָה֙ מִיָּדֶ֔ךָ וַֽיִּתְּנָ֖הּ לְרֵעֲךָ֥ לְדָוִֽד׃

passages.text: Because you did not obey the LORD or carry out His burning anger against Amalek, the LORD has done this to you today.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
God gave Saul a command.
God told Saul to destroy Amalek completely.
Saul did not obey God's voice.
Saul did not carry out God's fierce anger against Amalek.
Because Saul disobeyed, God punished him.
God did this to Saul today.
passages.original: כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹֽא־ שָׁמַ֙עְתָּ֙ בְּק֣וֹל יְהוָ֔ה וְלֹֽא־ עָשִׂ֥יתָ חֲרוֹן־ אַפּ֖וֹ בַּעֲמָלֵ֑ק עַל־ כֵּן֙ הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה עָשָֽׂה־ לְךָ֥ יְהוָ֖ה הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃

passages.text: Moreover, the LORD will deliver Israel with you into the hand of the Philistines, and tomorrow you and your sons will be with me. And the LORD will deliver the army of Israel into the hand of the Philistines.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD will give Israel into the power of the Philistines.
You, Saul, are the king of Israel.
You and your sons will fall to the Philistines tomorrow.
You and your sons will die and be with me, Samuel, in death.
The LORD will also give the army of Israel into the hand of the Philistines.
passages.original: וְיִתֵּ֣ן יְ֠הוָה גַּ֣ם אֶת־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֤ל עִמְּךָ֙ בְּיַד־ פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וּמָחָ֕ר אַתָּ֥ה וּבָנֶ֖יךָ עִמִּ֑י גַּ֚ם אֶת־ מַחֲנֵ֣ה יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל יִתֵּ֥ן יְהוָ֖ה בְּיַד־ פְּלִשְׁתִּֽים׃

passages.text: Immediately Saul fell flat on the ground, terrified by the words of Samuel. And his strength was gone, because he had not eaten anything all that day and night.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Samuel was a prophet who spoke God's words.
Samuel told Saul that God would punish him.
Saul heard Samuel's words.
Saul became very afraid.
Saul quickly fell flat on the ground.
Saul lost all his strength.
Saul had not eaten any bread that day.
Saul had not eaten any bread that night.
Saul was weak because he had not eaten.
passages.original: וַיְמַהֵ֣ר שָׁא֗וּל וַיִּפֹּ֤ל מְלֹא־ קֽוֹמָתוֹ֙ אַ֔רְצָה וַיִּרָ֥א מְאֹ֖ד מִדִּבְרֵ֣י שְׁמוּאֵ֑ל גַּם־ כֹּ֙חַ֙ לֹא־ הָ֣יָה ב֔וֹ כִּ֣י לֹ֤א אָכַל֙ לֶ֔חֶם כָּל־ הַיּ֖וֹם וְכָל־ הַלָּֽיְלָה׃

passages.text: When the woman came to Saul and saw how distraught he was, she said to him, “Look, your maidservant has obeyed your voice. I took my life in my hands and did as you told me.
passages.sermon:
The woman came to Saul.
She saw that Saul was very distraught.
She spoke to Saul.
She said, “Look, I am your maidservant.
I listened to your voice.
I obeyed what you told me.
I risked my life to do what you asked.”
passages.original: וַתָּב֤וֹא הָֽאִשָּׁה֙ אֶל־ שָׁא֔וּל וַתֵּ֖רֶא כִּי־ נִבְהַ֣ל מְאֹ֑ד וַתֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֗יו הִנֵּ֨ה שָׁמְעָ֤ה שִׁפְחָֽתְךָ֙ בְּקוֹלֶ֔ךָ וָאָשִׂ֤ים נַפְשִׁי֙ בְּכַפִּ֔י וָֽאֶשְׁמַע֙ אֶת־ דְּבָרֶ֔יךָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבַּ֖רְתָּ אֵלָֽי׃

passages.text: Now please listen to your servant and let me set a morsel of bread before you so you may eat and have the strength to go on your way.”
passages.sermon:
The woman spoke to Saul.
She was his servant.
She saw that Saul was weak and afraid.
She said, “Please listen to me.
Let me give you a piece of bread.
Eat the bread.
Then you will have strength.
You need strength to continue on your way.”
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֗ה שְׁמַֽע־ נָ֤א גַם־ אַתָּה֙ בְּק֣וֹל שִׁפְחָתֶ֔ךָ וְאָשִׂ֧מָה לְפָנֶ֛יךָ פַּת־ לֶ֖חֶם וֶאֱכ֑וֹל וִיהִ֤י בְךָ֙ כֹּ֔חַ כִּ֥י תֵלֵ֖ךְ בַּדָּֽרֶךְ׃

passages.text: Saul refused, saying, “I will not eat.” But his servants joined the woman in urging him, and he heeded their voice. He got up from the ground and sat on the bed.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul said, “I will not eat.”
Saul refused to eat.
Saul’s servants urged him to eat.
The woman also urged Saul to eat.
Saul listened to them.
Saul got up from the ground.
Saul sat on the bed.
passages.original: וַיְמָאֵ֗ן וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ לֹ֣א אֹכַ֔ל וַיִּפְרְצוּ־ ב֤וֹ עֲבָדָיו֙ וְגַם־ הָ֣אִשָּׁ֔ה וַיִּשְׁמַ֖ע לְקֹלָ֑ם וַיָּ֙קָם֙ מֵֽהָאָ֔רֶץ וַיֵּ֖שֶׁב אֶל־ הַמִּטָּֽה׃

passages.text: The woman had a fattened calf at her house, and she quickly slaughtered it. She also took flour, kneaded it, and baked unleavened bread.
passages.sermon:
The woman was in her house.
She had a fattened calf.
She acted quickly.
She slaughtered the calf.
She took some flour.
She kneaded the flour.
She baked unleavened bread.
passages.original: וְלָאִשָּׁ֤ה עֵֽגֶל־ מַרְבֵּק֙ בַּבַּ֔יִת וַתְּמַהֵ֖ר וַתִּזְבָּחֵ֑הוּ וַתִּקַּח־ קֶ֣מַח וַתָּ֔לָשׁ וַתֹּפֵ֖הוּ מַצּֽוֹת׃

passages.text: She served it to Saul and his servants, and they ate. And that night they got up and left.
passages.sermon:
The woman brought the food to Saul.
She also brought the food to Saul’s servants.
Saul ate the food.
Saul’s servants ate the food.
That night, Saul and his servants stood up.
They left that night.
passages.original: וַתַּגֵּ֧שׁ לִפְנֵֽי־ שָׁא֛וּל וְלִפְנֵ֥י עֲבָדָ֖יו וַיֹּאכֵ֑לוּ וַיָּקֻ֥מוּ וַיֵּלְכ֖וּ בַּלַּ֥יְלָה הַהֽוּא׃פ
